newsitem.title: UK: UK conservatives aim to keep tax and spending low.
newsitem.headline: UK conservatives aim to keep tax and spending low.

text.p: Britain's ruling Conservative Party on Wednesday put proposals to double living standards over 25 years and keep taxes low at the heart of its election campaign. Unveiling its manifesto for the May 1 election, the Conservatives pledged to reduce public spending to less than 40 pecent of national income over the five year life of the next parliament.

The Conservatives also said they would aim to hit their target of a 20 percent standard rate of income tax, compared with 23 percent in the 1997/98 financial year, and to maintain an inflation target of 2.5 percent or less.

"Our aim is to ensure Britain keeps the lowest tax burden of any major economy," the manifesto said. "The goal which we set ourselves in 1995 is to double living standards over 25 years. We are on course to achieve our goal."
